summary.intent: Plan and execute phase 63 (Read-Chain Navigation and Rotation Core) of the CipherBox project, then ship it via /ship-phase 63.
summary.outcome: Planning completed fully (7 plans across 4 waves, verification passed on iteration 2, all 7 requirements and 10 decisions covered). Execution reached Wave 2, plan 63-05 in progress at transcript end; /ship-phase 63 not yet reached.

repo: sdk-core has no `typecheck` script; the real type gate is `build` which runs `tsup && tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`. Plans 63-05 and 63-06 referenced a non-existent `typecheck` script and needed redirection.
Commit signing was already disabled repo-locally (commit.gpgsign: false); no biometric prompts expected during autonomous runs.
The GSD commit helper consistently reports a false-negative 'needs human verification' warning even on successful commits; git log is the authoritative check.
Worktrees are explicitly avoided for this phase due to documented pitfalls (node_modules leaks, api:generate conflicts) and tight cross-plan coupling on shared files like folder.test.ts.
CI health poll for the API uses `curl -fsS http://localhost:3000/health` on port 3000; the 63-07 plan had a fragile `sleep 12` that was replaced with this bounded poll loop.
The codebase map under .planning/codebase/ was stale (flagged by drift gate) but non-blocking at plan time since CONTEXT.md + RESEARCH.md carried precise current implementation-site references.
Phase 63 rotation engine landed in a dedicated engine.ts (513 lines, 83% coverage, 18 tests) with 4 named Phase-64 seams explicitly stubbed out.

code.finding: Replaced fragile `sleep 12` for API startup with a bounded health-poll loop mirroring CI's curl pattern against localhost:3000/health.
Open Questions section needed explicit (RESOLVED) markers — plan-checker treats unresolved open questions as a blocker even when answers are substantively present in the body.
Nyquist VALIDATION.md per-task verification map must be filled before plan-checker pass; leaving it as template placeholder triggers a warning.

workflow: GSD plan-checker iteration 1 returned 1 blocker + 2 warnings that were all artifact/formatting issues (not design flaws) and were fixed inline without replanning, then re-verified on iteration 2.
Pattern-mapper produced 10/10 analogs before the planner ran; this is the standard GSD flow and adds meaningful context without requiring a separate research pass.
Sequential main-tree execution (no worktrees) is the correct mode when plans share test files or barrel exports, even at the cost of parallelism.
API-SURFACE regeneration returned 0 symbols for this phase (pure internal sdk-core crypto, no public API changes) — safe to omit from planner context.
The execute-phase workflow's pre-execution gates (safe-resume, anti-patterns, branch check, STATE update) should all be run as a batch before dispatching any wave.

friction: GSD commit helper consistently emits a false-negative 'needs human verification' warning on every commit; requires a separate `git log` call to confirm success each time.
Plans 63-05 and 63-06 referenced a `typecheck` script that does not exist in sdk-core, requiring mid-execution redirection to `build`.
Plan-checker blocker on RESEARCH.md Open Questions was a pure formatting issue (missing RESOLVED markers), not a substantive gap — adds a full checker re-spawn cycle for a trivial fix.
Drift gate flagged stale codebase map but provided no actionable path to refresh it without blocking the planning pipeline.
open_items: Wave 2 plan 63-05 (hasCoveringGrant + zero-rotation invariant + barrel) was in progress at transcript end; Wave 3 (63-06) and Wave 4 (63-07 live e2e round-trip) not yet executed.
4 named Phase-64 seams stubbed in engine.ts need to be implemented in Phase 64.
Stale .planning/codebase/ map noted by drift gate — should be refreshed before the next phase that touches top-level config or shared infrastructure.
Plans 63-05 and 63-06 reference `typecheck` script — consider updating those PLAN.md files to use `build` so future executors don't need mid-execution correction.
